issues.label: Court authority over witness lists
issues.why: The court must apply MCR 2.401(I)(2) and its scheduling orders to decide whether amendment is permitted and on what terms.

issues.label: Good cause to amend witness list
issues.why: Plaintiff must show good cause for late substitution of an expert after the ordered deadlines.

issues.label: Prejudice from late expert substitution
issues.why: The court must assess prejudice to defendants (motion practice, facilitation, trial preparation) if Dr. Hall is added late.

issues.label: Diligence of plaintiff’s counsel
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether plaintiff acted diligently in prosecuting the case and managing expert availability/qualification.

issues.label: Bad faith or gamesmanship
issues.why: The court must consider whether the substitution/delay reflects strategic behavior (e.g., to avoid AOM challenge) rather than necessity.

issues.label: Dean v Tucker sanction factors
issues.why: If exclusion of the new expert effectively dismisses the case, the court must analyze the Dean factors before imposing that outcome.

issues.label: Proportionality of sanction
issues.why: The court must consider lesser sanctions (costs, adjournment, limited deposition) versus striking/excluding an expert.

issues.label: Effect on trial schedule
issues.why: The court must consider whether allowing amendment would require adjournments and disrupt the February 2023 trial date.

issues.label: Facilitation/ADR impact
issues.why: The court must address whether expert substitution undermines a meaningful facilitation process scheduled near discovery cutoff.

issues.label: Enforcement of deposition order
issues.why: The court must decide consequences for failure to produce Dr. Bal for deposition by the court-ordered deadline.

issues.label: Right to depose AOM affiant
issues.why: Defendants’ entitlement to depose Dr. Bal about his AOM statements and qualifications must be resolved.

issues.label: Discovery cutoff implications
issues.why: The court must determine whether discovery can/should be reopened to accommodate new expert discovery.

issues.label: Admissibility of late-disclosed expert
issues.why: The court must decide whether Dr. Hall can testify given late disclosure and potential violation of scheduling orders.

issues.label: Scope of permissible expert substitution
issues.why: The court must decide whether substitution is a true replacement or an expansion that changes opinions/claims.

issues.label: Affidavit of merit statutory compliance
issues.why: The court must decide if the AOM complied with MCL 600.2912d at filing (qualified physician, correct specialty/time devotion).

issues.label: AOM signer qualification timeframe
issues.why: The court must determine whether Dr. Bal devoted the required majority of professional time in the year preceding the alleged malpractice (2018-2019).

issues.label: Specialty match to defendant
issues.why: The court must ensure the AOM expert matches Dr. Lennox’s specialty as required under the expert-qualification statutes.

issues.label: Burden of proof on AOM validity
issues.why: Once challenged, the court must decide what evidence plaintiff must produce to create a factual issue that the AOM is valid.

issues.label: Use of extrinsic evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether it may consider transcripts/LinkedIn from other proceedings to evaluate AOM qualification disputes.

issues.label: Credibility vs. qualification
issues.why: The court must distinguish improper credibility attacks from permissible evidence showing statutory disqualification of the AOM affiant.

issues.label: Procedural vehicle for dismissal
issues.why: The court must determine the correct summary disposition rule and standard for an invalid AOM dismissal.

issues.label: Put up or shut up stage
issues.why: If discovery is closed, the court must apply the requirement that the nonmovant present admissible evidence supporting disputed facts.

issues.label: Consequence of invalid AOM
issues.why: The court must decide whether an invalid AOM requires dismissal and whether dismissal is with or without prejudice under Michigan law.

issues.label: Ability to cure defective AOM
issues.why: The court must decide whether plaintiff may cure by substituting a new expert/AOM after limitations have run or after filing.

issues.label: Relation back or tolling issues
issues.why: If amendment/new AOM is sought, the court must consider any tolling, savings, or relation-back doctrines affecting timeliness.

issues.label: Statute of limitations/repose
issues.why: Voluntary dismissal without prejudice may effectively bar refiling; the court must consider limitations and prejudice implications.

issues.label: Voluntary dismissal rule compliance
issues.why: The court must apply MCR 2.504(A) to decide whether plaintiff can dismiss without prejudice given answers/absence of stipulation.

issues.label: Court discretion on dismissal terms
issues.why: If dismissal is allowed, the court must decide terms/conditions (costs, fees, refiling conditions) to prevent unfair prejudice.

issues.label: Prejudice from dismissal without prejudice
issues.why: The court must assess whether dismissal would unfairly allow plaintiff to restart after defendants invested in discovery and motions.

issues.label: Timing of dismissal request
issues.why: The court must weigh proximity to dispositive motions, discovery deadlines, facilitation, and trial in deciding voluntary dismissal.

issues.label: Impact of pending summary disposition
issues.why: The court must consider whether voluntary dismissal should be denied to avoid evading an imminent merits-based dismissal ruling.

issues.label: Effect of striking amended witness list
issues.why: The court must decide whether striking the list was proper and whether it functionally bars plaintiff’s case without adequate analysis.

issues.label: Procedural defect of filing amendment
issues.why: The court must address plaintiff’s filing of an amended witness list without leave and its effect on admissibility and sanctions.

issues.label: Reconsideration standards
issues.why: The court must apply the proper standard for reconsideration (palpable error and different disposition) to prior rulings.

issues.label: Vicarious liability dependencies
issues.why: The court must consider whether claims against Tri County/Beaumont rise or fall with the underlying malpractice claim and expert proof.

issues.label: Separate defenses among defendants
issues.why: The court must ensure rulings (AOM validity, witness issues) are properly applied to each defendant’s posture and arguments.

issues.label: Case-management fairness
issues.why: The court must balance orderly administration and compliance with orders against deciding cases on the merits.

issues.label: Record adequacy for appellate review
issues.why: The court must make sufficient findings (especially on Dean factors, good cause, prejudice, sanctions) to support a correct decision.
